newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mostly firmer, volume light.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mostly firmer, volume light.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended higher Monday, with the exception of palladium, but volumes were light due to the Yom Kippur holiday.
But precious metals remain in a three week downtrend, with little sign of a bounce, though technical indicators look oversold, analysts said.

"Precious metals always look darkest before the dawn," Apostle Capital Management's New Jersey based fund manager, Andre DiMino, said. "The complex could be putting in a minor bottom, with the funds mostly out or short now, after the failure of last month upside break by silver."
COMEX December gold ended up 50 cents at $384.40 an ounce, after trading in a $383.80-384.70 range, following Friday's slide to a three year low for the December contract at $383.30.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $381.50/382.00, from the London afternoon fix at $381.00, and Friday's New York close at $381.75 which was a two month low.

"I think gold has been supported by some gold/silver spreading," DiMino added. The gold/silver ratio ended at 78.33, down from 78.55 Friday, but the ratio has recovered sharply from a low of 73.71 on August 26.
COMEX December silver ended up 3.20 cents at $4.895 an ounce, after trading in a $4.860-4.920 range. In the bullion market silver saw a fresh 18 month low around $4.80 early Monday.

"The complex feels oversold, with everyone bearish and the potential interest rate rise by the Fed at tomorrow's meeting already discounted into current prices, but there could be one more final washout to the downside," North American Equity Services floor trader John Geraghty said.

Investors had little incentive to buy gold while U.S. inflation remained low, the U.S. Federal Reserve was poised to move pre-emptively to tighten monetary policy, and the U.S. sharemarket and bond market remained healthy, analysts said.
But both gold and silver are now near the bottom of ranges that have provided value in the past two or three years, analysts noted.
NYMEX October platinum ended up 40 cents at $388.70 an ounce, but NYMEX December palladium ended down $1.80 at $119.00.
In London early Monday, palladium fixed at a fresh three year low at $116.75 an ounce.

Slow demand from the Japanese electronics industry, concerns over weakening offtake by the auto sectors in the U.S. and Europe and expectations of more Russian supply pressure are depressing the platinum metals group, analysts said. -Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk, +1-212-859-1641 email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
